what: The 12 study basins as GIS layers (outlines, gauges, elevation, land cover) in results/gis_layers/, exported from the sources of results/basin_gis.json with the clipping rule of code/07_basin_maps.py, and checked against results/basin_gis.json and the CAMELS attribute table. Deliverable D3 of the mid-term plan.
disclosure: Claude Code wrote and ran this script under the team lead's direction (first run 2026-10-29; revised after the independent review; this run 2026-11-01 14:28); the team's own check of these layers is not done.
disclosure_independent_review: An independent AI reviewer agent (Claude) recomputed these layers on 2026-10-30 (results/review_gis_layers.json); the team's own check of these layers is not done.

independent_review.who: the same independent AI reviewer agent (Claude) as in round 1, started again at the coordinator's request; no right to edit the project except code/review/gis_layers/ and this file; the layers were written and revised by a different AI agent session (Claude Code) directed by the team lead

parameters.clipping: a cell belongs to the basin when its centre lies inside the outline (rasterio geometry_mask, all_touched=False), as in code/07_basin_maps.py

known_note_from_basin_gis: Elevation: our mean differs from CAMELS elev_mean by +1.6 m in the median, but by more than 25 m in: Catawba, NC +47 m, French Broad, NC +100 m, South Toe, NC +163 m. Averaging our grid to coarser cells (up to 920 m) moves our mean by at most 2.5 m, so grid size does not explain this. The elev_mean field stored in the outline file is close to ours (mean absolute difference 8.4 m, largest -24.7 m, South Toe, NC). We cannot tell from the CAMELS documentation why its table is lower in these basins; the ranking of the basins is nearly the same (rank correlation 0.99) and the landscape classes of 01_data_audit.py (mountain = mean elevation above 600 m) are unchanged with our elevations.

notes: 12 basins, 29 files, 9.4 MB; every raster was reopened after writing and its bounds checked against the outline.
The GeoPackage stores its write time, so its sha256 changes on every run; the GeoTIFFs and GeoJSON files are deterministic.
Nothing is downloaded by this script; a missing tile or land-cover file stops it (code/07_basin_maps.py fetches them).
